title: Design: A/R Detail links and plain numbers match the design picture
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The organization has open documents in these reports at two locations, {Location-A} and {Location-B}, and you are enrolled at both; {Location-A}'s name comes first in A to Z order.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
  • Customer {Customer-A} has an open invoice made at {Location-B}, customer {Customer-B} an unused credit memo at {Location-A}, and customer {Customer-C} an open invoice at {Location-A}, all more than 90 days past due.
    For example: {Customer-A} is ZZAUTOTEST D-63 Oakland City, {Customer-B} is ZZAUTOTEST D-63 Sledge and {Customer-C} is ZZAUTOTEST D-63 Wellington.
  • Starting screen: A/R Detail (Reports, then "A/R Aging Detail" under ACCOUNTS RECEIVABLE in the left menu) is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu in light theme at 100% zoom, with the "91 or more days past due" bucket expanded.
  • The design picture "Links only where they can open" (ar-ap-p5-links-only-where-they-can-open.png) is attached to this case and open beside the browser at 100% zoom; compare the layout, labels and styles, not the names and amounts, which are only examples.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Compare the header row with the picture.
  2. Look at {Customer-A}'s invoice number.
  3. Look at {Customer-B}'s credit memo number.
  4. Look at {Customer-C}'s invoice number.
  5. Compare the subtotal row at the end of the bucket with the picture.
  6. Widen the browser window to 1536 px and look across the page.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the chevron, then the columns in the picture's order: Date, Location, Transaction type, ID, Customer full name (with a small up arrow), Due date, Amount, Open balance; this report has no Past due column (capital letters: D-04 and D-81).
  • Step 2: a blue link: another location you work at.
  • Step 3: plain dark text, not blue.
  • Step 4: a blue link.
  • Step 5: "Total for 91 or more days past due" with the Amount and Open balance sums in bold.
  • Step 6: nothing overlaps, is cut off or clipped; the layout is the same as at 1440 px.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11531 (Story 1, Reports open in QuickBooks name order), story SV-11532 (Story 2, Sort by clicking any column header), story SV-11537 (Story 7, Document links open where they can)

  • S7-R1: “A document number is a link only when the user has the permission to open it and can open it in its own location; otherwise it shows as plain text.”
  • S7-R3: “An invoice or part sale at another location the user is enrolled in shows the existing location-switch prompt on the report, before leaving it: title "Switch location?", message "This work order is in {location}. Switch your active location to view it?" (for a part sale: "This part sale is in {location}. Switch your active location to view it?"), buttons "Switch location" and "Cancel".”
  • S7-R10: “A/R credit memos and deposits show as plain text: they have no page of their own.”
  • S2-R1, A/R Detail columns: “A/R Detail: Date, Location (when shown), Transaction type, ID, Customer full name, Due date, Amount, Open balance.”
  • S1-R5: “A/R Detail and A/P Detail keep their aging buckets in this fixed order: "91 or more days past due", "61-90 days past due", "31-60 days past due", "1-30 days past due", "Current". Inside each bucket, rows open in customer or vendor name order (S1-R2 to S1-R4), ties by document number (S2-R4).”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "A/R and A/P Report Sorting" (https://claude.ai/artifact/BRYCdjKwGRSgGPC9xxkgF4), read 22 Oct 2026: page 5 "Document links and Switch location" (board Links.dc.html). Compare the screen with the pictures below at 100% zoom; the expected results still come from the PRD quotes above, the pictures give the look and the on-screen labels.

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • ar-ap-p5-links-only-where-they-can-open.png: figure "Links only where they can open" (This build (after)), board "5. Document links and Switch location (SV-5706)"
  • ar-ap-p5-every-invoice-number-is-a-link.png: figure "Every invoice number is a link" (Production (before)), board "5. Document links and Switch location (SV-5706)" (today's look, for comparison only)

The design's own words:

  • "A number links only with the right permission and a location the user works at; otherwise plain text. Native link style. S7-R1, S7-R2, S7-R6, S7-R7, S7-N1, S7-N2." (caption of "Links only where they can open")
  • "Signed in to Heavy Duty, the Lethbridge invoices (S3-) are links too." (caption of "Every invoice number is a link")

Difference from the PRD (DD-01): the PRD says buttons "Switch location" and "Cancel" (S7-R3), title "Switch location?"; the design shows buttons "Cancel" (left, grey) then "Switch Location" (right, blue, capital L), and a close "×" at the top right of the dialog; caption: "Switch Location opens it there.". This case follows the PRD; the difference is question 11 on Chris Ward's question sheet (added 22 Oct 2026); the design version is held in D-76.

Difference from the PRD (DD-06): the PRD says A/R Detail and A/R Collection headings written "Transaction type", "Customer full name", "Due date", "Past due", "Open balance" (S2-R1); the design shows the after pictures read "Transaction Type", "Customer Full Name", "Due Date", "Past Due", "Open Balance"; today's production pictures already read the same, with "Location Full Name". This case follows the PRD; the difference is question 4 on Chris Ward's sheet (sent 22 Oct 2026); the design version is held in D-81.
